abstract: The main driver of inequality--returns on capital that exceed the rate of economic growth--is again threatening to generate extreme discontent and undermine democratic values. Thomas Piketty's findings in this ambitious, original, rigorous work will transform debate and set the agenda for the next generation of thought about wealth and inequality.

Full narrative

Capital in the Twenty-First Century by Thomas Piketty was published by Harvard University Press in 2014. Conceptually, the work connects to Inequality, Capital (architecture), Democracy, Work (physics) and Economics. The book was recognised: Financial Times and Goldman Sachs Business Book of the Year Award (2014). The book was recognised: Spear's Book Award Shortlist (Business, 2014).

OpenAlex records 13,766 citations. That places it in the top 1% of works in its field and year of publication. Citations peaked in 2019 with 1572 citing works. Notable citing venues include Cambridge University Press eBooks, SSRN Electronic Journal and Palgrave Macmillan UK eBooks. Of the citation statements scite has classified, 27 support its claims and 4 contradict them. The citing works include 7,418 journal articles, 3,846 book chapters and 1,036 preprints. They come from 40 countries, led by the United States, the United Kingdom and Germany. The citation record includes 3 formal book reviews.

In teaching, it is assigned in 2 course reading lists, listed in 3 open course syllabi and discussed in 3 recorded lectures. It is recorded in 19 library collections. Its subject matter aligns with No poverty among the Sustainable Development Goals.
